comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body: u/Sweet-Chip6849 could you please add details on how AI was used to make this? Rule 4 is there to make sure promotional posts contribute by getting into the process and actual development. There's a real risk of the sub being swamped by self-promotion with nothing to discuss otherwise. If you don't update, this post may be removed.

replies.author: Sweet-Chip6849
replies.body:
Thanks for the heads-up! Reddit isn't letting me edit the original post, so I'll explain the development process here.

FLOW FIRE BODYCAM is being developed using Claude Opus and DeepSeek, with Godot and Blender.

I direct the project, make the creative decisions, test the gameplay, and decide which improvements to keep. The AI agents handle the coding and technical implementation.

We've also built a custom testing system that allows the agents to launch the game, record gameplay, measure weapon and camera movement, detect problems, and compare changes.

Recently, we've been working on making the weapons, arms, and bodycam feel physically connected, improving recoil, aiming, movement, and visual realism.

The goal is to keep improving the game through actual testing and iteration, not just generating code.

I'll be sharing more of the development process as the project evolves!
